full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 1-3-2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court' Division in Civil Revision No. 2809 of 2006 discharging the Rule. 

 2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.33 of 2000 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Comilla, for declaration that the judgment and decree obtained by respondent No.1 in Title Suit No.215 of 1987 is collusive, ineffective and without jurisdiction. 

 3. The plaintiffs case, in-short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Labonaya Prova Lodh, who left for India back in 1957. The Government acquired 0.341/2 acre of land for the plaintiff from Comilla Zilla Samabaya Union in LA Case No. 2/88-89 and handed over the possession thereof to him on 30-8-1968. Meanwhile, the plaintiff constructed a two storied building as per the approved plan of Comilla Pourashava in one part of the suit land and established a printing press in the other part. His further case is that the suit land was enlisted as enemy property in EPL Case No. 8 of 73-74. Defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 211 of 1980 in the Court of the then Munsif, Second Court, Comilla, which was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Comilla and renumbered as Title Suit No. 215 of 1987 against the admitted owner Labonaya Prova Lodh for specific performance of contract and the present plaintiff was impleaded as defendant No. 9. The plaintiff and the Government contested the suit by filing separate written statements. The suit was dis-missed on contest by the judgment and order dated 30-11-1988. 

 4. Against the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, defendant No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 51 of 1989 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. On transfer, the appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Second Court, Comilla, who by his judgment and order dated 30-11-1991 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 5. Against which, the plaintiff and the Additional Deputy Commissioner filed two revisional applications before the High Court Division and obtained Rules in Civil Revision Nos. 874 and 1594 of 1992 respectively. The High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 26-11-1996 discharged both the Rules. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiff filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 4 of 1999 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner; Comilla filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 5 of 1999 before this Division. This Division upon hearing dismissed both the civil petitions. Against which, the plaintiff and the Government filed Civil Review Petition Nos. 31 and 32 of 1999 which were also rejected on 2-3-2000. 

 7. The plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 213 of 1999 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla, plaint of which was also rejected allowing the application filed by defendant No.1 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Subsequently, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 33 of 2000 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Comilla, for declaration that the suit property is abandoned property and the judgment and decree obtained in Title Suit No. 215 of 1987 is void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Simultaneously, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Comilla also filed Title Suit No. 32 of 2000 on the self-same prayer. 

 8. Plaintiff No. 1 appeared in the suit and filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. The plaintiff contested the application filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure by filing written objection. 

 10. Against the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge, defendant No. 1 filed Civil Revision Nos. 58 and 59 of 2004 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. On transfer, both the civil revisions were heard analogously by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Comilla, who allowed both the revisions on 7-5-2006. 

 11. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and order dated 7-5-2006 passed in Civil Revision No. 59 of 2004, the plaintiff filed a revisional application before the High Court Division in which Rule was issued in Civil Revision No. 2809 of 2006. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by his judgment and order dated 1-3-2009 discharged the Rule. 

 12. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the plaintiff-leave petitioner has filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division. 

 13. Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner, submits that the learned Additional District Judge rejected the plaint of both the suits as those suits were barred under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure although there is no scope for rejection of the plaint under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the High Court Division also affirmed that judgment as such, the impugned judgment should be set-aside. 

 16. The High Court Division came to a finding that the trial Court failed to appreciate the law and facts involved in the suit and wrongly rejected the applications filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the nature and character of earlier Title Suit No. 215 of 1987 and those of subsequently filed Title Suit Nos. 32-33 of 2000 were not same and that the learned Additional District Judge rightly observed that the averments made in the subsequent suits were sufficient for rejection of the plaints of both the suits. 

 17. The High Court Division also observed that the learned District Judge disposed of two revisions, Civil Revision Nos. 58 and 59 of 2004 and that the plaintiff being aggrieved by the judgment of Civil Revision No. 59 of 2004 obtained a Rule from it and that the petitioner did not file any revisional application against the impugned judgment so far as it relates to Civil Revision No. 58 of 2004 which weakened the case of the petitioner. 

 18. What is important to note here is that the learned Additional District Judge rejected the plaints of both the suits as according to him those were barred under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This is not the correct exposition of law. The plea of res judicata is to be decided after framing an issue to that effect. There is no scope for application of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of plaint. 

 19. Having gone through the plaints of both the suits, we are of the view that the plaints of both the suits were rightly rejected by the learned Additional District Judge but that should have been done by resorting to the provision of section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the plaints of both the suits shall be deemed to have been rejected under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the materials on record justify to do so. 

 Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.
